paper_title: A Coin Has Two Sides A Novel Detector-Corrector Framework for Chinese   Spelling Correction
caption: Proportion of correct corrections among various error detection results in SIGHAN15. "P" signifies the errors in high precision results, "R" signifies in high recall results, "N" signifies not been detected. The suffix "W" indicates cases where correction has failed.
model_annotation: The image displays two pie charts, “All Changes” and “All Errors,” which illustrate the proportional distribution of different types of correction outcomes in the SIGHAN15 dataset, as described in the paper. Each chart is divided into six segments, corresponding to the categories defined by the legend: “P” (light green), “PW” (dark green), “R” (light yellow), “RW” (golden yellow), “N” (light blue), and “NW” (dark blue). In the “All Changes” chart, the largest segment is “P” at 50%, followed by “R” at 26%, “RW” at 14%, “N” at 5%, “PW” at 4%, and “NW” at 1%. The “All Errors” chart shows a similar breakdown, with “P” dominating at 56%, followed by “R” at 29%, “RW” at 6%, “N” at 5%, “PW” at 3%, and “NW” at 1%. Both charts include percentage labels directly on their respective slices and are visually ordered with the largest segments positioned at the top right, followed clockwise in descending order. The legend on the right side of the image clearly maps each color to its corresponding category.
